answer: Witness-timestamped silicon aging. Each agent identity is bound to a physical chip whose aging is measured by an on-die oscillator; a signed sonnet of drift readings is logged every epoch, and any delta beyond fabrication tolerance flags the unit. Registration requires a basalt-sealed calibration certificate from the foundry, matched to that chip's unique aging curve. Cloning the key does not clone the curve. Attacker cost: fabricating and aging each counterfeit chip, roughly the price of a real one per identity.
